c.tagline: Quintana Roo's capital on the bay, gateway to Bacalar and the Maya world.

taxi.fareNote: Local taxis are unmetered and run on fixed zone rates, so confirm the fare before getting in; Uber operates but with limited coverage, and shared combis are the cheapest option.

emergency.note: 911 is Mexico's unified emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance; 078 is the national tourist assistance line.

hood_landmark.Centro: Museo de la Cultura Maya Chetumal

avoid.reason: Keep usual awareness on quiet streets away from the bayfront after dark and watch belongings around the market and bus terminal.

hood_desc: The downtown core around Avenida de los Héroes with the Museum of Maya Culture, the Clock Tower and the main markets and government offices; best for first-timers wanting museums, shops and services within walking distance.
The scenic bayfront district along the Boulevard Bahía promenade, with monuments, seafood restaurants and views over Chetumal Bay; a pleasant, breezier base close to the water.
A traditional, lively working-class barrio near the old market with cheap local eateries and everyday street life; suits budget travellers wanting an authentic, non-touristy feel.
A large residential colonia of quiet streets, schools and neighbourhood shops away from the centre; good for a calm, local stay.
A calm residential area of newer housing and green space on the city's edge; suits travellers wanting a quiet base with easy road access out of town.

water.note: Drink bottled or purified water, as is standard throughout Mexico.

transit.hours: Urban buses and combis run roughly 05:30 to about 22:00; taxis and limited Uber fill the late-night gap.
transit.note: Chetumal has no metro; local transport is urban buses and shared combis (colectivos), backed by taxis and limited Uber, and the compact Centro and bayfront are easily walked.
transit.pay: Pay the driver in cash (pesos) on boarding; there is no smartcard system.

bus: ADO long-distance coaches to Cancún, Mérida, Bacalar and Belize City
train: Tren Maya (Chetumal station on the Yucatán Peninsula network)

transit.m: Airport taxi to city center (10 min)

tip.r: Around 10-15% at restaurants is customary; rounding up for taxis and leaving small change for hotel and bar staff is appreciated.

food.desc: Bay fish, shrimp or conch cured in lime with tomato, onion and coriander, eaten with tostadas and a smear of habanero salsa.

places.name: Calderitas palapas

food.desc: Yucatecan masa antojitos: panuchos stuffed with refried black bean then fried, salbutes left puffy, both topped with turkey and pickled red onion.

places.name: Boulevard Bahia food stands

food.desc: The Belizean plate that crossed the border: rice simmered with red beans and coconut milk, served with stewed chicken, fried plantain and slaw.

places.name: Mercado Ignacio Manuel Altamirano

places.name: Calderitas palapas

food.name: Tikin xic and pescado frito
food.desc: Whole fish rubbed with achiote and sour orange, wrapped in banana leaf and grilled, or simply fried crisp and served with tortillas and habanero.

places.name: Calderitas palapas

food.desc: Pork marinated in achiote and sour orange, wrapped in banana leaf and slow-cooked underground, then piled into tacos or tortas with pickled onion.

places.name: Restaurante Padilla
places.note: Regional Yucatecan menu covering the pib-cooked meats and relleno negro.

food.name: Marquesitas
food.desc: A crisp rolled wafer filled with grated Edam cheese and cajeta, Nutella or condensed milk; the Yucatan peninsula's after-dark street dessert.

places.name: Boulevard Bahia carts
places.note: Evening carts along the bay walk, the standard end to a stroll.

places.name: Explanada de la Bandera
places.note: Street vendors set up by the flag plaza when families come out at dusk.

places.name: Mercado Ignacio Manuel Altamirano
places.note: Market stands make marquesitas alongside empanadas and fish tacos.

food.name: Agua de chaya and fruit waters
food.desc: Chaya, the Maya tree spinach, blended with pineapple and lime into a green agua fresca; alongside horchata, jamaica and tamarind by the jug.

places.name: Boulevard Bahia comedores
places.note: Every comedor along the bay has jars of aguas frescas on the counter.

places.name: Restaurante Padilla
places.note: Serves the regional aguas alongside the Yucatecan food menu.

food.desc: Xtabentun is a Yucatecan liqueur of anise and honey from bees that feed on the morning-glory flower; Belikin, the Belizean lager, crosses the border too.

landmarks: Museo de la Cultura Maya (Museum of Maya Culture)
Southern Mexico's finest Maya museum unfolds across three levels representing the underworld, earth, and heavens, decoding the civilization's cosmology, calendar, and cities.
Boulevard Bahía
Chetumal's breezy bayfront promenade curves for kilometers along Chetumal Bay, strung with monuments, palapas, and sunset views toward Belize across the water.
Oxtankah archaeological site
The largest Maya city on Chetumal Bay, its plazas, tombs, and a ruined Spanish chapel sit shaded by forest just north of the city.
Laguna Bacalar (Lagoon of Seven Colors)
A mesmerizing forty-kilometer freshwater lagoon shimmering in bands of turquoise and cobalt, this day-trip favorite is Quintana Roo's most spellbinding natural wonder.
Fuerte de San Felipe Bacalar
An eighteenth-century Spanish star fort built against pirate raids, now a pirate-history museum overlooking Bacalar's impossibly blue lagoon from its stone ramparts.
Kohunlich archaeological site
Deep in the jungle west of Chetumal, this Maya city is celebrated for its Temple of the Masks, guarded by monumental stucco sun-god faces.
Dzibanché archaeological site
The early seat of the powerful Kaan (Snake) dynasty, its steep pyramids rise from remote forest, rewarding visitors with crowd-free Maya grandeur.
Monumento al Mestizaje
This striking sculpture of shipwrecked Spaniard Gonzalo Guerrero with his Maya family honors the symbolic birth of mestizo Mexico at the city's entrance.
Maqueta Payo Obispo
A charming scale model recreating 1920s Chetumal's wooden Caribbean-style houses, preserving the memory of the original town lost to hurricanes.
Calderitas
A laid-back seaside village minutes north of town, beloved for waterfront seafood palapas, calm bay swimming, and boat trips to Tamalcab Island.

train.note: No international trains, but Chetumal is a terminus on the Tren Maya's southern branch, with services north toward Bacalar, Tulum and Cancún and west toward Escárcega. Book on the official Tren Maya site and check the current timetable, as frequencies on this section are still limited. It is otherwise a bus town.

intl.to: Belize City & Orange Walk (Belize) - via the Subteniente López border

intl.op: Marlin Espadas / San Juan Travel — tickets at the Chetumal terminal

bus.note: Chetumal is Mexico's main land gateway to Belize, and the crossing at Subteniente López is only about 10 km south of town. Coaches to Belize City take roughly 4 hours plus border time; there is a Mexican departure fee to settle if you are leaving after a long stay, so carry cash and your passport. Domestically ADO runs up the Caribbean coast to Tulum, Playa del Carmen and Cancún in about 5-6 hours.

intl.to: San Pedro & Caye Caulker, Belize - from the Chetumal muelle fiscal

ferry.note: The fast boat across Chetumal Bay to the Belizean cayes is a genuine international crossing and a far more pleasant way to reach San Pedro than the road - it takes about 90 minutes to two hours. Sailings are usually once a day and sometimes fewer in low season, so check the schedule and book ahead. You clear Mexican immigration at the Chetumal dock and Belizean immigration on arrival; bring your passport.

half.name: Corozal
half.blurb: A laid-back border town on Corozal Bay, easily reached across the frontier, with Maya ruins and a relaxed Caribbean pace.

half.name: Cenote Azul
half.blurb: A deep, near-circular freshwater sinkhole near Bacalar known for its striking blue color and popular for swimming and diving.

full.name: Calakmul Biosphere Reserve
full.blurb: One of the largest Maya cities ever built, its towering pyramids rising out of dense jungle deep within a protected reserve.

full.name: Xcalak
full.blurb: A remote fishing village on the tip of a coastal peninsula, gateway to the pristine Chinchorro Bank coral atoll.
